AND YET THE COMPLETE READ IS NOT A SUPERSET OF THE CAPPED ONE, WHICH IS THE FINDING OF THIS SECTION. Against the file the 2026-11-06 run committed (2,328 of 2,336 rows, capped TRUE), today's read GAINED 19 rows and LOST 6: BODALCHEM (score 9 - the only TRADE candidate of that day and the card that was published from it), INDIAGLYCO (4), GSPCROP (3), ONEPOINT (2), INDOCO (1) and SHARVAYA (1). The earlier read is preserved in git at b917f12:docs/ideas/scan/2026-11-06.json. The newer file is committed because it is a net gain of 13 rows and it surfaced two candidates the 6-Nov run never saw.

*** CORRECTION, FOUND LATE IN THIS RUN AND THE MOST IMPORTANT TECHNICAL FINDING IN IT: THERE WAS A TRADING SESSION ON SUNDAY 2026-11-08 AND THE SCAN CANNOT SEE IT. *** The Diwali Muhurat session traded on 8-Nov-2026 and BSE published a bhavcopy for it: BhavCopy_BSE_CM_0_0_0_20261108_F_0000.CSV, fetched in this run, HTTP 200, 247,944 bytes, TradDt '2026-11-08' on every row, 4,685 STK rows all with volume above zero and total turnover of Rs 2,685 cr (a normal Friday's file, 2026-11-06, is 268,934 bytes). score.py sees that session because it prices from BSE's per-scrip endpoint: 54 of the 75 rows in the rebuilt track.json carry last_date '2026-11-08' and the other 21 are names that did not trade in the one-hour session.

SCAN.PY DOES NOT SEE IT, AND THE REASON IS ONE LINE OF CODE. scripts/ideas/bse.py line 84, inside bhavcopy(): 'if d.weekday() >= 5: return None' - a weekend date is rejected WITHOUT the URL being tried. nse_bhavcopy() has the identical guard at line 120. So every builder that walks bhavcopies (scan.py, and by the same path breakout.py) treats a Saturday or Sunday session as non-existent: the scan's as-of came out as 2026-11-06, its 65-day window is short by one real session, and no scan file exists for 2026-11-08 at all. This is reported, not fixed - scripts/ideas/*.py is outside this routine's write scope.

SO WHAT DID THE SESSION ACTUALLY CONTAIN? Measured by hand, because the scan could not. BSE's whole-day announcement list for 2026-11-08 was read in full - 75 rows of the 75 BSE itself reports - of which 26 fall in the 1,214-name universe, and for 2026-11-09 the list has 2 rows, both newspaper publications. Of the 26, fifteen are newspaper publications or trading-window closures, four were already swept onto cards in this run (Rajesh Power's analyst-meet outcome, South West Pinnacle's press release and investor presentation, Oriental Rail's LoA), two are board-meeting intimations (ARVAYA, PGFOILQ), one is a volume clarification the playbook skips (TVSELECT) and one a transcript (PATELRMART). FOUR WERE OPENED AND ALL FOUR DECLINED, each for a stated reason:

- FRATELLI VINEYARDS (541741, Rs 540.0 cr) - revised board outcome of 7-Nov with Q2/H1 FY27 results. Consolidated revenue Rs 45.24 cr in Q2 FY27 against Rs 45.88 cr in Q2 FY26, i.e. **-1.4% YoY**; H1 Rs 89.96 cr against Rs 82.39 cr, +9.2%; FY26 Rs 181.29 cr. The triage bar for a results trigger is revenue growth of at least 30% with PAT growth; a quarter with revenue down 1.4% does not reach it, so no further reading was done. The outcome also appoints Mr Avinash Gautam Thadani (DIN 03497176) an additional director.
- ZEELEARN (533287, Rs 200.8 cr) - cessation of Mr Manish Rastogi (DIN 10056027) as Whole-time Director and CEO on attaining superannuation, effective 8-Nov-2026. The playbook's triage explicitly skips promoter and director changes.
- SAURASHTRA CEMENT (502175, Rs 540.2 cr) - a show-cause notice under section 74(5) of the CGST / Gujarat GST Act from the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, Unit-86, Porbandar. A tax notice is a red flag, not an idea trigger.
- A B INFRABUILD (544281, Rs 776.8 cr) - a 45-page 'Press Release on Overview of the Business and Financials of the Company'. A general corporate overview is not an event with a number attached, which is exactly what the triage list says to skip.

CONCLUSION, MEASURED: the Muhurat session carried no candidate-grade filing in the universe, so skipping the filings research for it costs nothing TODAY. The defect still matters, because the same line of code will silently drop any future weekend session - and will keep every scan window one session short until it is fixed.

GS Products India had initiated proceedings against the company before the MSME Facilitation Council, Aligarh, with a claim of approximately Rs 12.50 crore; the company argues the additional disputed amount of about Rs 1.81 crore was below its materiality threshold of Rs 3.26 crore, and SEBI observed that the aggregate claim of about Rs 12.50 crore exceeded that threshold, so the dispute should have been disclosed. The matter was placed before the board on 5-Nov-2026 and disseminated with the board outcome.

DECLINED on two grounds. The playbook's triage skips anything whose trigger is not a hard operational number, and a regulatory warning is the opposite of one - it is a reason to be more careful about this filer's disclosure, not a reason to research it as an idea. And the ORDER classification is simply wrong: there is no order in this document, so the candidate exists because of a classifier error, logged in data_problems.
